newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish yields seen 22 bps over Bunds in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Finnish yields seen 22 bps over Bunds in EMU.

text.p: Finnish 10-year bond yields are seen trading 22 basis points over Bunds if both Finland and Germany are among the first countries to enter the third phase of EMU at the start of 1999, according to a Reuters poll.
If Finland did not join Economic and Monetary Union in the first wave the 10-year yield premium over Germany was seen at 80 bps.
At 1430/1230 GMT, the Finnish/German 10-year bond yield gap was 62 basis points.

In the poll, 22 analysts, dealers and economists at banks and corporate treasury departments were asked to forecast the Euro-denominated 10-year Finnish/German yield spread if both Finland and Germany are among the first countries joining EMU.
The mean of the forecasts was 22 basis points and they ranged from five bps to 60.
Most (18 of the 22 respondents) saw the spread between 10 and 30 bps, while two participants expected it to be inside 10 bps. Two saw spreads wider than 30 bps.

If Finland remained outside monetary union, the mean of the forecasts was that 10-year government markka bonds would yield 80 basis points over German Euro-denominated paper. The forecasts ranged from 27 to 130 bps.
Most (19) put the differential between 50 and 100 bps, two expected it to be over 100 bps and one saw it at 27 bps.
The poll was carried out on Thursday last week. Forecasts were collected on an anonymous basis. @
